Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum with real simple roots (so $a_{ii}=2$ for
every color $i$), a field $k$ placed in degree zero, and weighted-homogeneous
KLR polynomials $Q_{jk}$ satisfying (Q1)-(Q4) as in
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]; write
$b_{jk}=d_j a_{jk}=b_{kj}$. Fix a color $i$. The **minimal-parabolic KLR
diagram proof category** $\mathcal P_i$ is the additive graded $k$-linear
2-category of weighted oriented diagrams described by the generators, objects
and equations below.

**Generators and composition.** The objects are the weights
$\mu\in P$. The generating $1$-morphisms are the downward generators
$G_j:\mu\to\mu-\alpha_j$, one for every color $j$, and the single upward
generator $H_i:\mu\to\mu+\alpha_i$. Horizontal composition reads chronological
negative words from the vacuum outward. Take additive sums of objects and
grading shifts, and use idempotent completion when speaking of word
projectives. The generator $H_i$ denotes **normalized projective
restriction**: in the polynomial flag realization at input weight $h=\langle
h_i,\mu\rangle$ it is basic reversed flag restriction shifted by
$-d_i(1+h)$; it is distinct from unshifted basic restriction.

**The graded 2-morphism spaces.** The weights are 0-objects. A 1-morphism
is a finite composable word in the $G_j,H_i$, with its specified source and
target weights; identities are empty words. For parallel words $u,v$, define
$\operatorname{Hom}^n(u,v)$ as the degree-$n$ part of the $k$-span of formal
oriented string diagrams generated by the dots, downward crossings and four
units/counits below, modulo the displayed local relations. Every strand is
labeled by its color, and its direction is downward for $G_j$ and upward for
$H_i$. The top boundary is the source word and the bottom boundary the target
word. Regions carry the unique weights obtained from the outside source
weight by the indicated simple-root changes. Diagrams are generic: transverse
double crossings, isolated dots and nondegenerate cups/caps, with no triple
crossing or dot at a crossing/extremum. Oppositely oriented crossings denote
the specified adjunction mates of a downward crossing, not new generators.
Use planar isotopies preserving the ordered oriented local events; moving
a crossing past an extremum uses the mate relations below. Vertical
composition is stacking and horizontal composition is juxtaposition at a
common weight; degrees add under either operation. The interchange relation
and bilinearity are imposed. A degree-$n$ map from $u$ to $v$ is a degree-zero
map $u\{n\}\to v$ with the internal-shift convention of the grading supplier.
Additive sums, shifts and idempotent completion have their usual graded
2-category meanings applied to these Hom spaces.

**Degrees and the native crossing.** Dots have degree $2d_j$ and downward
crossings have degree $-b_{jk}$, matching the grading of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]]. The native crossing is
$\tau$, with native equal-color divided difference
$(f-sf)/(x_1-x_2)$; for expressing the source diagram equations put
$\kappa=-\tau$ for **every** color pair, retaining dots, idempotents and $Q$.
Thus the native cubic braid numerator is globally opposite to the source
numerator, while the quadratic $Q$ is unchanged. Impose the full downward KLR
relations of the cited Definition.

**Adjunctions and the rank-one matrix.** At input $i$-weight $h$, the first
unit $1\to H_iG_i$ and the second counit $H_iG_i\to1$ have degree
$d_i(1-h)$; the first counit $G_iH_i\to1$ and the second unit
$1\to G_iH_i$ have degree $d_i(1+h)$. Impose both adjunction triangles with
their adjacent input-weight shifts and cyclicity of the dot. For $h\ge0$
prescribe the degree-zero rank-one matrix
$$H_iG_i\cong G_iH_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{h-1}1\{d_i(1-h+2r)\};$$
for $h<0$ prescribe
$$G_iH_i\cong H_iG_i\oplus\bigoplus_{r=0}^{-h-1}1\{d_i(1+h+2r)\}.$$
The off-diagonal crossing component is the cup--source-crossing--cap
transfer, and the identity columns and rows are the indicated dotted
units/counits. Adjoin its actual inverse blocks, requiring both matrix inverse
equations; the dotted dual rows and columns are the finite triangular
coefficient convolution determined by bubble inversion, and the crossing
block satisfies the local cross-and-cap equations. In particular, at $h<0$,
if $r_h:G_iH_i\to H_iG_i\oplus D_{-h}$ is this matrix, then $r_h^{-1}j_H$ and
$p_Hr_h$ are the specified natural inclusion and projection with product
$1_{H_iG_i}$.

**Explicit rank-one inverse blocks.** Put $P=G_iH_i$, $V=H_iG_i$
at the common outside weight $\mu$, and write
$\eta_\mu:1_\mu\to H_iG_i$, $\varepsilon_\mu:G_iH_i\to1_\mu$
for the first adjunction and
$\eta'_\mu:1_\mu\to G_iH_i$, $\varepsilon'_\mu:H_iG_i\to1_\mu$
for the second. Let $\tau^{GG}$ be the native equal-color downward crossing
and $\tau^{HH}$ its twofold adjunction mate. Fix the native sideways mates by
$$T=(H_iG_i\varepsilon_\mu)(H_i\tau^{GG}H_i)(\eta_\mu G_iH_i),\qquad S=(G_iH_i\varepsilon'_\mu)(G_i\tau^{HH}G_i)(\eta'_\mu H_iG_i).$$
Their middle words are respectively $H_iG_iG_iH_i$ and
$G_iH_iH_iG_i$; the displayed final counits consume their rightmost
$G_iH_i$ and $H_iG_i$. Thus $T:P\to V$ and $S:V\to P$ are typed,
with degree $d_i(1-h)-2d_i+d_i(1+h)=0$. The source-crossing
component in the preceding rank-one matrix is $-T$. For $h\ge0$, its
identity columns are $C_k=x^k\eta_\mu$, and its identity rows are
$$R_k=\sum_{a+j=h-1-k}A_{\mu,j}\,\varepsilon'_\mu x^a,\qquad 0\le k<h,$$
where $a,j\ge0$. The matrix is $\rho=(-T,(C_k)_k):P\oplus D_h\to V$
and its specified inverse is $\sigma=(S,(R_k)_k):V\to P\oplus D_h$.
Impose both equations $\sigma\rho=1$ and $\rho\sigma=1$; in components
these say $-ST=1_P$, $R_kT=0$, $SC_k=0$, $R_kC_\ell=\delta_{k\ell}$
and $-TS+\sum_kC_kR_k=1_V$. For $h<0$, take
$C^-_k=x^k\eta'_\mu$ and
$$R^-_k=\sum_{a+j=-h-1-k}\mathsf H_{\mu,j}\,\varepsilon_\mu x^a,\qquad 0\le k<-h,$$
again with $a,j\ge0$. Now
$\rho=(-T,(R^-_k)_k):P\to V\oplus D_{-h}$ and
$\sigma=(S,(C^-_k)_k):V\oplus D_{-h}\to P$; impose
$\rho\sigma=1$, $\sigma\rho=1$. Equivalently $-TS=1_V$,
$TC^-_k=0$, $R^-_kS=0$, $R^-_kC^-_\ell=\delta_{k\ell}$ and
$-ST+\sum_kC^-_kR^-_k=1_P$. The shift summands $D_h,D_{-h}$ are
exactly those displayed above. The row degrees are respectively
$d_i(h-1-2k)$ and $-d_i(1+h+2k)$, opposite the column degrees, so every
matrix component is degree zero after the indicated shifts. Empty identity
sums at $h=0$ give the same inverse equations. These are imposed relations
in the presentation; a claim that the concrete flag bimodules satisfy them
still requires their local realization proof.

**Bubble series and slides.** The normalized far-left bubble series
$A_\mu(t),\mathsf H_\mu(t)$ have constant coefficient $1$ and satisfy
$A_\mu(t)\mathsf H_\mu(t)=1$. Genuine negative-degree bubbles vanish. The $A$
coefficient with index $m$ is the clockwise bubble with $-h-1+m$ dots when
this count is nonnegative, extended by formal inverse coefficients otherwise;
its degree is $2d_im$. The other family has dot count $h-1+\ell$ and degree
$2d_i\ell$. Impose the finite-coefficient slides verified on the monic flag
model: adjoining an $i$ root $z$ divides $A$ by $(1-zt)^2$ and multiplies
$\mathsf H$ by that factor; adjoining a spectator root $y$ of color $j\ne i$
multiplies $A$ by
$q_{ij}^{\mathrm{rev}}(y,t)=t^{-a_{ij}}Q_{ij}(t^{-1},y)/t_{ij}$, where $t_{ij}$
is the nonzero extremal coefficient, and divides $\mathsf H$ by it. Every
reciprocal coefficient is defined by the finite recursion with constant
coefficient $1$.

**Four oriented same-color equations.** The following notation specifies
actual local diagrams, all with color $i$. The two-crossing equations have
common outside weight $\mu$; the single curls have the adjacent region
weights specified individually below.
Read tangent directions in the page. Let $C_L,C_R$ be the cap arch
(two bottom endpoints and no top endpoints), whose tangent at its peak
points left or right, respectively. Their bottom arrows, from left to
right, are $(\downarrow,\uparrow)$ and
$(\uparrow,\downarrow)$. Let $U_L,U_R$ be the cup valley
(two top endpoints and no bottom endpoints), whose tangent at its trough
points left or right; their top arrows are
$(\uparrow,\downarrow)$ and $(\downarrow,\uparrow)$.
An exponent on $C$ or $U$ counts dots on its open arc. Let $B_{\mathrm{ccw}}^b$
and $B_{\mathrm{cw}}^b$ be the counterclockwise and clockwise bubbles
with literal dot count $b$, located to the right of the cap/cup in the outside
region of weight $\mu$. Their negative dot counts are exactly the fake
bubbles defined by the coefficient conventions above, not zero by convention.
Write $\eta_\mu:1_\mu\to H_iG_i$ and
$\varepsilon'_\mu:H_iG_i\to1_\mu$ for the first unit and second counit,
and $\eta'_\mu:1_\mu\to G_iH_i$, $\varepsilon_\mu:G_iH_i\to1_\mu$
for the second unit and first counit. Let $\tau^{HH}$ be the twofold
adjunction mate of the native equal-color downward crossing. Define
$$L_\mu=(H_i\varepsilon'_\mu)(\tau^{HH}G_i)(H_i\eta_\mu),\qquad R_\mu=(\varepsilon_\mu H_i)(G_i\tau^{HH})(\eta'_\mu H_i).$$
The first formula starts and ends at $H_i$ with input $\mu$; the second
starts and ends at $H_i$ with input $\mu-\alpha_i$. Thus both units and
counits in $L_\mu$ have degree $d_i(1-h)$, while those in $R_\mu$ have
degree $d_i(1+h)$. The crossing degree $-2d_i$ makes their degrees
$-2d_ih$ and $2d_ih$ respectively. Products in these formulas apply the
rightmost map first, with adjacent weights determined by composition.
Geometrically $L_\mu$ is an upward-strand curl with its loop bulging LEFT and
its left-adjacent region of weight $\mu$. This is an endomorphism of
$H_i$ at input $\mu$, and its bubble on the right-hand side is in the
left region $\mu$. Let $R_\mu$ be the upward-strand curl with its loop
bulging RIGHT and its right-adjacent region of weight $\mu$. Its left
region is $\mu-\alpha_i$, so it is an endomorphism of $H_i$ at input
$\mu-\alpha_i$, and its bubble is in the right region $\mu$.
Both have one native crossing and the two extremal turns of the loop.
Let $D_{\downarrow\uparrow}$ and $D_{\uparrow\downarrow}$ be the two
opposite crossing mates composed in the two orders on their indicated
straight boundaries, with common outside region $\mu$. Impose
$$L_\mu=\sum_{a+b=-1}x^aB_{\mathrm{ccw},\mu}^b,\qquad R_\mu=-\sum_{a+b=-1}x^aB_{\mathrm{cw},\mu}^b,$$
$$D_{\downarrow\uparrow}=-1_{\downarrow\uparrow}+\sum_{a+b+c=-2}C_L^aB_{\mathrm{cw},\mu}^bU_R^c,$$
$$D_{\uparrow\downarrow}=-1_{\uparrow\downarrow}+\sum_{a+b+c=-2}C_R^aB_{\mathrm{ccw},\mu}^bU_L^c.$$
Composition in the last two displays is top-to-bottom: $U$ first, then
the outside bubble, then $C$. The single-curl equations are upward-strand
endomorphism equations; their cup/cap forms are their specified adjunction
mates, not cap drawings with unspecified endpoint arrows. In every sum,
$a,c$ on open strands are nonnegative. The clockwise bubble with literal
$b$ dots is the $A_\mu$ coefficient of index $b+h+1$, and the
counterclockwise bubble is the $\mathsf H_\mu$ coefficient of index
$b-h+1$, where $h=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$. Coefficients of negative index
are zero and the index-zero coefficient is one. The nonnegative coefficient
and open-dot indices make each sum finite. The opposite-crossing equations
have degree zero: their correction degrees are
$2d_i(1-h)+2d_i(a+b+c+h+1)=0$ and
$2d_i(1+h)+2d_i(a+b+c-h+1)=0$. The two curls have degrees
$-2d_ih$ and $2d_ih$ at their respective, different input weights.

The native single-crossing signs follow from $\kappa=-\tau$; two-crossing
signs are unchanged. The literal triple-dot sum is $-2$, not the compact
$-1$ printed in Webster's Figure 2: in the full positive-weight equation,
coefficient indices satisfy $f_1+f_2+f_3=h-1$ and the bubble has literal
count $b=-h-1+f_2$, giving $a+b+c=-2$; the negative-weight equation uses
$g_1+g_2+g_3=-h-1$ and $b=h-1+g_2$, giving the same value. Reflection
exchanges the two bubble orientations and preserves region weights. The
single-curl coefficient sums instead have total $h$ or $-h$, yielding
literal $a+b=-1$. At $h=0$ the triple sums are empty and the single
curls are respectively $+1$ and $-1$ on their specified shifted input
weights. At the $h=1$, $p(u)=u$ vacuum, $H_iG_i=k$, $G_iH_i=0$,
$A_\mu=1$ and the only surviving clockwise bubble has $b=-2$; thus the
first cancellation is $0=-1_k+1_k$, with no degree or vacuum contradiction.

**Distinct-color crossing mates.** For $j\ne i$, at input weight $\mu$
put $\xi=\mu+\alpha_i-\alpha_j$, so $X=G_jH_i$ and $Y=H_iG_j$
both go from $\mu$ to $\xi$. Let $\tau^{G_iG_j}:G_iG_j\to G_jG_i$
and $\tau^{G_jG_i}:G_jG_i\to G_iG_j$ denote the two native downward
crossings. Specify the handed pair by the actual typed mate composites
$$a=(H_iG_j\varepsilon_\mu)(H_i\tau^{G_iG_j}H_i)(\eta_\xi G_jH_i):X\to Y,$$
$$b=(\varepsilon'_\xi G_jH_i)(H_i\tau^{G_jG_i}H_i)(H_iG_j\eta'_\mu):Y\to X.$$
The intermediate words are respectively $H_iG_iG_jH_i$ and
$H_iG_jG_iH_i$; in $a$ the final first counit consumes the rightmost
$G_iH_i$, while in $b$ the final second counit consumes the leftmost
$H_iG_i$. Impose $ba=t_{ij}1_X$ and $ab=t_{ij}1_Y$ for this same handed
pair. Thus $a$ and $t_{ij}^{-1}b$ are mutually inverse and give
$H_iG_j\cong G_jH_i$, commuting with the $j$ dot. If
$h=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$, both composites have degree
$d_i(1+h)+d_i(-1-h+a_{ij})-b_{ij}=0$. Replacing both native crossings by
the source crossings $\kappa=-\tau$ negates $a$ and $b$ separately and
leaves both cancellation scalars unchanged.

There is no $H_j$ in this minimal category. The analogous calculation in
the separately distinguished category $\mathcal P_j$ has scalar $t_{ji}$
in both orders for its own handed pair. That does not assign $t_{ji}$ to
the other composition of the fixed pair $a,b$ above. Comparing the two
partial actions, or asserting a full double-right-mate ratio, requires the
separate coherent assembly proof; it is not an additional relation imposed
here.

**Status of the relations.** These equations are relations of this proof-tool
category. Their consistency and homogeneous realization are established by
the polynomial flag model
([[lem-minimal-parabolic-polynomial-flag-model-realizes-the-graded-diagram-relations]]),
rather than assumed for the actual cyclotomic induction/restriction action; no
claim about the latter is made here. This definition uses no choice: it is a
presentation by generators and homogeneous equations, and every sl(2) infinite
family appearing in the matrix and bubble clauses is a finite coefficient
recursion from a constant coefficient $1$.

Fix a color $i$ and the formal proof category of
[[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], on a symmetrizable real
Cartan datum with finite index set and arbitrary field $k$. Use the native KLR
parameters of
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], degrees of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], the PBW convention of
[[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]], and the nil-Hecke matrix/idempotent convention
of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. Then the polynomial
flag construction described below realizes all the defining graded diagram
relations of that formal category, including its rank-one cross/cap,
bubble-slide/inversion and mixed-color cup/cap relations; it asserts a
representation of the formal proof category, not faithfulness or a cyclotomic
quotient identification.

**The model.** Choose a color order with $i$ last. For spectator alphabets
$Y_j$ of sizes $m_j$ ($j\ne i$) put $C=\bigotimes_{j\ne i}k[Y_j]^{S_{m_j}}$,
$r=m_i$, $A_{ij}=-a_{ij}$,
$t_{ij}=[u^{A_{ij}}]Q_{ij}(u,v)\in k^\times$,
$q_{ij}=Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$, and choose a monic framing polynomial $a_i(u)$ of
degree $\lambda_i\geq0$; initially its coefficients have their universal homogeneous
degrees, so all formulas are graded, and the standard specialization is
$a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. Set
$$p_m(u)=a_i(u)\prod_{j\ne i}\prod_{y\in Y_j}q_{ij}(u,y),\qquad N=\lambda_i+\sum_{j\ne i}A_{ij}m_j,\qquad h_m=N-2r,$$
and $c_r(u)=u^r-e_1u^{r-1}+\cdots+(-1)^re_r$. The vertex ring $L_m$ is the
monic factor ring for $p_m=c_rb_{N-r}$, equivalently $C[e_1,\ldots,e_r]$ modulo
all coefficients beyond degree $N-r$ of the monic expansion $p_m/c_r$; it is
finite free over $C$ of rank $\binom Nr$ and is zero for $r>N$. Its $i$ flag is
$B_m=L_m[z]/b_{N-r}(z)$, free of rank $N-r$ over $L_m$ and rank $r+1$ over
$L_{m+i}$, with the target root alphabet obtained by adjoining $z$. The
underlying spectator flag is $C_m^j=L_m[y]$; its target action appends $y$ to
$Y_j$ and replaces $p_m$ by $p_mq_{ij}(u,y)$.

**The shifts and generators.** Every downward generator carries the ordered
shift $s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell$. Thus
$G_i=F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ is the $B_m\{-2d_ir\}$ tensor functor; $G_j$ for
$j\ne i$ is the $C_m^j\{s_j(m)\}$ tensor functor. The basic reversed $i$ flag
is $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}=B_m\otimes_{L_{m+i}}-$ without a shift, whereas the
formal upward generator at INPUT vertex $m$ is
$H_i(m)=E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(m)\{-d_i(1+h_m)\}$. These are distinct
conventions. The basic flags have degree-zero
$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\{t_i(m)\}\dashv F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$, where
$t_i(m)=-2d_i(h_m-1)$. At vertex $m$ the formal first unit and second cap have
degree $d_i(1-h_m)$, and the formal first cap and second unit have degree
$d_i(1+h_m)$.

**The four maps and the Casimir.** All four maps are the explicit dual-basis
maps of the two monic coefficient forms on $B_m$: $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}:B_m\to
L_m$ extracts $z^{N-r-1}$ and has degree $-2d_i(N-r-1)$;
$\tau_{\mathrm{new}}:B_m\to L_{m+i}$ extracts $z^r$ and has degree $-2d_ir$.
The first cap is $b_1\otimes b_2\mapsto\tau_{\mathrm{new}}(b_1b_2)$ and the
first cup is its dual-power-basis Casimir; the second cap and cup use
$\tau_{\mathrm{old}}$. For a monic polynomial $f$ their Casimir is the
polynomial kernel $K_f(X,Y)=(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ in the two-root quotient.

**Crossings, colors and bubbles.** Source crossings are
$\kappa=-\tau_{\mathrm{native}}$ for EVERY color pair. Source equal-color
operators are $(s-1)/(X-Y)$; source unequal operators are the switch/quotient
in the increasing-color direction and switch times $Q$ in the reverse
direction. Thus native operators are their negatives, and both actual crossing
degrees are $-b_{jk}$ with the ordered shifts above. On the $i,j$ pair the
successive underlying rings are
$D_1=L_m[y,z]/(b(z)q_{ij}(z,y))$ and $D_0=L_m[y,z]/b(z)$, with source maps
$\pi:D_1\to D_0$ and $f\mapsto Q_{ij}(z,y)f:D_0\to D_1$; the actual
handed pair $a:G_jH_i\to H_iG_j$, $b:H_iG_j\to G_jH_i$ of the
formal Definition satisfies $ba=t_{ij}1_{G_jH_i}$ and
$ab=t_{ij}1_{H_iG_j}$. Thus $a$ and $t_{ij}^{-1}b$ are mutually inverse.
Native minus signs negate both source mates and preserve both cancellation
scalars. Full comparison with a separately distinguished $j$-adjunction
belongs to coherent assembly, rather than to this category with only $H_i$. The basic isomorphism $E_iG_j\cong(G_jE_i)\{-b_{ij}\}$ holds,
and the normalized formal $H_iG_j\cong G_jH_i$ is unshifted.

**Realized equations.** The canonical rank-one $\rho$ and its prescribed second-mate and finite
coefficient-convolution inverse of
[[lem-cyclotomic-polynomial-flag-comparison-has-the-prescribed-second-mate-inverse]], the
same-color cross/cap equations, the bubble series
$\Phi_i(u)=p_m(u)/c_r(u)^2$ and its reciprocal, and the finite-coefficient
bubble-slide identities are realized by the stated polynomial maps. In
particular the normalized positive $h$ identity columns have degrees
$d_i(1-h+2k)$ for $0\le k<h$, and the negative branch uses the inverse
crossing plus the dot/cap rows. All polynomial pairings and relations persist
after arbitrary monic coefficient specialization as UNGRADED identities; such
a specialization does not assert nilpotence, a homogeneous trace degree, or a
highest-weight $K_0$ claim. No geometry, characteristic restriction, or
one-dimensional-Hom hypothesis is imposed.

Let $p(u)$ be monic of degree $N\geq0$ over a commutative ring $D$. Let $L_r$ be the monic factor ring $p=c_rb_{N-r}$, where $c_r$ is monic of degree $r$, and put $L_r=0$ for $r<0$ or $r>N$. Put
$$B_r=L_r[z]/b_{N-r}(z)=L_{r+1}[z]/c_{r+1}(z),\qquad h=N-2r.$$
Use the native nil-Hecke crossing $\tau=(1-s)/(X-Y)$ of [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], dots of degree $2d$, and the matrix idempotent convention of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. Induction is $G(r)=B_r\{-2dr\}\otimes_{L_r}-$, basic restriction is the reversed $B_{r-1}$ tensor functor, and normalized restriction at input $r$ is $H(r)=B_{r-1}\{-d(1+h)\}\otimes_{L_r}-$. The first adjunction uses the coefficient form $\tau_{\rm new}:B_r\to L_{r+1}$ extracting $z^r$; the second uses $\tau_{\rm old}:B_r\to L_r$ extracting $z^{N-r-1}$. Units are the trace-dual power-basis Casimirs. Write $\eta:1\to HG$, $\varepsilon:GH\to1$, $\eta':1\to GH$, $\varepsilon':HG\to1$ for these maps, at their indicated input weights.

Set $P=GH$, $V=HG$ at input $r$. Define the actual native mates, rather than freely adjoined inverses, by
$$T=(HG\varepsilon)(H\tau^{GG}H)(\eta GH):P\to V,\qquad S=(GH\varepsilon')(G\tau^{HH}G)(\eta'HG):V\to P,$$
where $\tau^{HH}$ is the twofold first-adjunction mate of $\tau^{GG}$. Put
$$A(t)=t^h\frac{b(t^{-1})}{c(t^{-1})},\qquad \mathsf H(t)=A(t)^{-1},\qquad A_0=\mathsf H_0=1.$$
Coefficients with negative index are zero. For $h\geq0$, let $C_k=x^k\eta$ and
$$R_k=\sum_{a+j=h-1-k}A_j\varepsilon'x^a\quad(0\leq k<h).$$
Then the actual flag bimodule maps $\rho=(-T,C):P\oplus D_h\to V$ and $\sigma=(S,R):V\to P\oplus D_h$ satisfy
$$-ST=1_P,\quad R_kT=0,\quad SC_k=0,\quad R_kC_\ell=\delta_{k\ell},\quad -TS+\sum_kC_kR_k=1_V.$$
For $h<0$, set $C^-_k=x^k\eta'$ and
$$R^-_k=\sum_{a+j=-h-1-k}\mathsf H_j\varepsilon x^a\quad(0\leq k<-h).$$
The maps $\rho=(-T,R^-):P\to V\oplus D_{-h}$ and $\sigma=(S,C^-):V\oplus D_{-h}\to P$ satisfy
$$-TS=1_V,\quad TC^-_k=0,\quad R^-_kS=0,\quad R^-_kC^-_\ell=\delta_{k\ell},\quad -ST+\sum_kC^-_kR^-_k=1_P.$$
Here $D_h=\bigoplus_{k<h}1\{d(1-h+2k)\}$ and $D_{-h}=\bigoplus_{k<-h}1\{d(1+h+2k)\}$. At $h=0$ both sums are empty.

These maps also give the two typed upward curls

derivations.claim: A finite planar routing schedule. Forget dots temporarily and count all transverse intersections, including self-intersections, by $C$. An arc with a self-intersection has an innermost monogon or bigon; two simple arcs with more intersections than their endpoint alternation requires have a bigon. To see the latter, cut along one arc: successive entrances and exits of the other arc in the resulting disk either delimit a bigon or delimit a subarc containing a self-intersection, to which the first case applies. A closed component similarly has a monogon, a bigon with another component, or is a simple disjoint circle: cut along a path from the circle to the exterior and use successive entrances and exits. Clear the chosen disk as follows. An interior arc returning to the same side cuts off a smaller disk; choose that disk first. Otherwise its segment joins two sides, and push the disk corner past its nearest intersection by a triangle move. This removes that intersection from the chosen disk. A whole closed component in the disk is handled first by the same procedure. Thus the number of intersection vertices on or inside the chosen disk, apart from its defining corners, strictly decreases on every main triangle move, until its monogon or bigon is empty. This is a finite schedule: the diagram has finitely many vertices, and selection of a smaller disk strictly decreases that number too. Local extrema are carried along by isotopy; a crossing carried past an extremum is its specified adjunction mate. No new crossing pair is inserted. Once every component is simple and every pair crosses at most once, cut the disk along one component at a time and repeat the same nearest-intersection triangle sweep to route that component to its chosen reduced path. The already routed components remain fixed; the number of unrouted components decreases. This gives a finite sequence of triangle moves between reduced drawings of the same matching.

Algebraic use of the schedule. A triangle move is a downward KLR braid equation or its adjunction mate. Its leading term has the same three crossings, and every correction has fewer crossings. An empty downward bigon is reduced by the quadratic KLR equation; an opposite-orientation bigon is reduced by the prescribed cancellation equation, whose correction has no crossings but may insert a cup and cap. A monogon is reduced by the appropriate curl equation or its adjunction mate, removing its one crossing. Distinct-color opposite bigons have their specified unit cancellation. Move dots along components by cyclicity and the KLR dot equations; every correction again has fewer crossings. Induct first on $C$. At a fixed $C$ use the finite disk schedule of step 1.1, and apply the induction hypothesis separately to each correction. All sums are finite: curl and cancellation coefficients have nonnegative open-dot and bubble indices with fixed total. In particular an inserted cup and cap cannot defeat this induction, since its branch has already lowered $C$. After intersections are reduced, extra extrema on a simple component cancel by the triangles; these decrease the finite extremum count without changing $C$. Move each isolated circle to the far left by the coefficient slides, in decreasing order of its distance from the left edge. For a fixed coefficient every slide is a finite polynomial identity; it creates no intersection and decreases that distance. Replace the reciprocal bubble family by its finite inverse-coefficient recursion. Finally route the reduced open matching as in step 1.1, handling its shorter-crossing corrections by induction, and place the dots at the chosen positions. This proves finite spanning by the stated normal forms; it does not presuppose their independence.

Leading matching coefficients in the actual model. Work over the universal framing ring and then its generic splitting fraction field, localizing distinct root differences and the finitely many nonzero spectator $Q$ values used in the diagram. This is permitted solely to find a nonzero witness, not to prove an identity by specialization. Use the flag summands in which every background or visited $i$ root is a distinct root of the free universal framing polynomial. These summands are indexed by root additions and removals and are one-dimensional over the splitting fraction field. They exist because $r$ may grow while the framing degree grows as $2r+h-A_{\mathrm{spect}}$. The spectator factors of $p$ need not be separable: they are placed entirely in the complementary factor, and their values at these free framing roots are nonzero. Chinese remainder against the separable free framing factor gives the indicated summands even when a spectator factor has repeated roots. A dot multiplies by that root. A native equal-color crossing is $(1-s)/(x-y)$: its root-switching term has coefficient $-1/(x-y)$, and its other term retains the labels and deletes that crossing. A distinct-color crossing switches the labeled roots with coefficient either a unit or a nonzero $Q$ value. The monic coefficient cap at a simple root $z$ has coefficient $1/f'(z)$ up to its specified unit normalization, and its dual cup has the inverse coefficient; these follow by evaluating the dual-power Casimir $(f(X)-f(Y))/(X-Y)$ on the root idempotents. All these coefficients are nonzero. Consequently expanding a reduced matching diagram on these summands has a leading term that carries a root label along each of its matched components, with a nonzero product coefficient. All other terms delete at least one crossing, and hence are smaller in the minimal crossing number of their boundary matching after step 2.1. Choose pairwise distinct free framing roots for the different open $i$ components and independent spectator roots for the other components. The endpoint equalities of this leading term specify exactly its matching: a different matching must identify two labels assigned to different components. In a finite proposed relation select a matching of maximal minimal crossing number. No smaller matching can contribute to its root-labeled leading coefficient, and another matching of the same crossing number has different endpoint equalities. Its coefficient is therefore its dot polynomial on the selected component roots times its bubble polynomial, times a nonzero rational factor. This replaces an invalid independent bending of interior upward endpoints; only the explicit root flags and their already proved cup/cap maps are used.

A faithful witness at a fixed physical weight. Let $h=\langle h_i,\mu\rangle$ be fixed, choose spectator background counts $m_j$, and put $A_{\mathrm{spect}}=\sum_{j\ne i}(-a_{ij})m_j$. For increasing $r$ put $N=h+2r$ and $\lambda_i=N-A_{\mathrm{spect}}$. Choose the universal monic framing $a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}+z_1u^{\lambda_i-1}+\cdots+z_{\lambda_i}$ with $\deg z_s=2d_is$, independent of the root variables. In the flag model, $p=a_i\prod_{j\ne i}Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$ and $\mathcal B=p^{\mathrm{rev}}/(c_r^{\mathrm{rev}})^2=a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}U$ with $U_0=1$. Its first $D$ coefficients have the unit triangular form $\mathcal B_s=z_s+\sum_{0<\ell<s}z_\ell U_{s-\ell}+U_s$ for $s\le D$ whenever $\lambda_i\ge D$. Thus substituting bubbles in any nonzero finite downward PBW/bubble combination leaves a nonzero polynomial-operator combination before truncation. By the faithful polynomial representation it has a test vector with nonzero output. Take a homogeneous component of that vector and output, and let $B$ bound their degrees and all framing indices used. These bounds can be fixed while $r$ grows: only the finitely many appended strand variables, bubble indices, and fixed-degree symmetric background coefficients occur in the operator and test vector. Let $L$ bound the number of appended $i$ flags. Every flag/factor coefficient relation encountered has degree at least $2d_i(h+r-L+1)$; all variables have nonnegative degrees. Choose $r$ with $\lambda_i\ge D$ and this bound greater than $B$. No nonzero output of degree at most $B$ can belong to the ideal of these higher-degree relations, so it survives in that actual flag model. For the general-boundary leading coefficient of step 3.1, choose $r$ also large enough to supply distinct free framing roots for every component and at least $D$ unused free complementary roots. Basis and confluence. Step 2.1 gives spanning at all boundaries, and steps 3.1–4.1 prove independence in the actual model at all boundaries. Forced vacuum coefficients. Write $h_\ell$ for the counterclockwise bubble coefficient with literal $\lambda_i-1+\ell$ dots, with $h_0=1$ and $h_{\ell<0}=0$. Closing the marked relation $a_i(x)x^{\ell-1}=0$, for $\ell\ge1$, is lawful in $J$ and gives $h_\ell+c_{i,\lambda_i-1}h_{\ell-1}+\cdots+c_{i,0}h_{\ell-\lambda_i}=0$. Thus $\mathsf H_\Lambda a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}=1$ and $A_\Lambda=a_i^{\mathrm{rev}}$. Let $S$ be this coefficient-specialization ideal; then $S\subset J$. The basis of step 5.1 shows that specializing these far-left central coefficients alone leaves the ordinary downward corner exactly $R(\beta)$. This conclusion concerns $S$ alone and does not assume the conclusion about $J$. For $\lambda_i=0$, $a_i=1$ kills the first $i$ word and the same recurrence gives $A=\mathsf H=1$.

The correctly typed local closure. Work modulo $S$. A straight vacancy closure with $q\ge0$ dots has clockwise $A$-index $\lambda_i+1+q$, so is zero. The crossed closure on the first physical $G_i$ at input $\Lambda$ is the first-adjunction mate of $R_\Lambda$, whose $H_i$ input is $\Lambda-\alpha_i$ and whose clockwise bubble region is $\Lambda$. In its exact native equation the bubble literal count is $b=-\lambda_i-1+m$ and $a+b=-1$, hence $a=\lambda_i-m$. Its value is consequently $-\sum_{m=0}^{\lambda_i}A_mx^{\lambda_i-m}=-a_i(x)$; its degree is $2d_i\lambda_i$. Taking the mate preserves this polynomial because the dot is cyclic. Before these closures, slide any bubble at the bent source $\Lambda+\alpha_i$ across the added root $z$: $A_{\Lambda+\alpha_i}=(1-zt)^2A_\Lambda$ and the reciprocal equation for $\mathsf H$. Each coefficient is finite, so this reduces it to polynomial dots and the already specialized vacuum coefficients. No bubble is assigned the wrong ambient weight.

The marked operator at the dominant vacuum. Modulo the killed-upward ideal, the actual positive rank-one matrix identifies $H_iG_iv_\Lambda$ with $D_{\lambda_i}$. Its columns are $v_r=x^r\eta$, $0\le r<\lambda_i$, and its dual rows are the finite bubble-weighted counit rows of the prescribed inverse. A raw row with $s\ge0$ extra dots sends $x^rv_0$ to $h_{r+s-\lambda_i+1}$. Its value on $a_i(x)v_0$ is therefore the zero recurrence of step 6.1 at index $s+1$. Every actual dual row is a finite combination of raw rows, so all projections of $a_i(x)v_0$ vanish; the matrix inverse equation implies the column itself is zero. Multiplying by powers of $x$ kills $a_i(x)$ on all columns and hence on $H_iG_iv_\Lambda$. When $\lambda_i=0$ this object is already zero. Every killed-upward factor. A term through $W H_iv_\Lambda$ has factor maps $f:G_uv_\Lambda\to W H_iv_\Lambda$ and $g:W H_iv_\Lambda\to G_vv_\Lambda$. Bend that vacuum $H_i$ in both maps. The triangles recover $gf$ by closing the composite of the bent maps, which has all-downward boundaries with an additional first $i$ strand at source $\Lambda+\alpha_i$. The interior word $W$ need not be downward. Apply step 5.1 to the composite and then the coefficient slide of step 7.1. Put $n=|\beta|$ and let $W_P\subset S_{n+1}$ fix position one. There are two double cosets, $W_P$ and $W_Ps_1W_P$. Removing the distinguished input and output and inserting them in their required positions supplies length-additive representatives $u s_1v$, $u,v\in W_P$, in the second case; the first case uses only $s_2,\ldots,s_n$. Choose these reduced words for PBW. Shorter braid corrections still straighten in this family. In the first case the first strand closes to the zero straight vacancy loop. In the second the exterior words fix position one, whose color is $i$ at both boundaries; therefore both colors at the unique $s_1$ crossing are $i$. Fix a color $i$ and the formal proof category of
[[def-minimal-parabolic-klr-diagram-proof-category]], on a symmetrizable real
Cartan datum with finite index set and arbitrary field $k$. Use the native KLR
parameters of
[[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], degrees of
[[def-klr-grading-and-diagrammatic-composition]], the PBW convention of
[[thm-klr-pbw-basis-theorem]], and the nil-Hecke matrix/idempotent convention
of [[def-divided-power-klr-idempotents-and-projectives]]. Then the polynomial
flag construction described below realizes all the defining graded diagram
relations of that formal category, including its rank-one cross/cap,
bubble-slide/inversion and mixed-color cup/cap relations; it asserts a
representation of the formal proof category, not faithfulness or a cyclotomic
quotient identification.

**The model.** Choose a color order with $i$ last. For spectator alphabets
$Y_j$ of sizes $m_j$ ($j\ne i$) put $C=\bigotimes_{j\ne i}k[Y_j]^{S_{m_j}}$,
$r=m_i$, $A_{ij}=-a_{ij}$,
$t_{ij}=[u^{A_{ij}}]Q_{ij}(u,v)\in k^\times$,
$q_{ij}=Q_{ij}/t_{ij}$, and choose a monic framing polynomial $a_i(u)$ of
degree $\lambda_i\geq0$; initially its coefficients have their universal homogeneous
degrees, so all formulas are graded, and the standard specialization is
$a_i(u)=u^{\lambda_i}$. Set
$$p_m(u)=a_i(u)\prod_{j\ne i}\prod_{y\in Y_j}q_{ij}(u,y),\qquad N=\lambda_i+\sum_{j\ne i}A_{ij}m_j,\qquad h_m=N-2r,$$
and $c_r(u)=u^r-e_1u^{r-1}+\cdots+(-1)^re_r$. The vertex ring $L_m$ is the
monic factor ring for $p_m=c_rb_{N-r}$, equivalently $C[e_1,\ldots,e_r]$ modulo
all coefficients beyond degree $N-r$ of the monic expansion $p_m/c_r$; it is
finite free over $C$ of rank $\binom Nr$ and is zero for $r>N$. Its $i$ flag is
$B_m=L_m[z]/b_{N-r}(z)$, free of rank $N-r$ over $L_m$ and rank $r+1$ over
$L_{m+i}$, with the target root alphabet obtained by adjoining $z$. The
underlying spectator flag is $C_m^j=L_m[y]$; its target action appends $y$ to
$Y_j$ and replaces $p_m$ by $p_mq_{ij}(u,y)$.

**The shifts and generators.** Every downward generator carries the ordered
shift $s_j(m)=-2d_jm_j+\sum_{\ell>j}(-b_{j\ell})m_\ell$. Thus
$G_i=F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ is the $B_m\{-2d_ir\}$ tensor functor; $G_j$ for
$j\ne i$ is the $C_m^j\{s_j(m)\}$ tensor functor. The basic reversed $i$ flag
is $E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}=B_m\otimes_{L_{m+i}}-$ without a shift, whereas the
formal upward generator at INPUT vertex $m$ is
$H_i(m)=E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}(m)\{-d_i(1+h_m)\}$. These are distinct
conventions. The basic flags have degree-zero
$F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\dashv E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$ and
$E_i^{\mathrm{basic}}\{t_i(m)\}\dashv F_i^{\mathrm{basic}}$, where
$t_i(m)=-2d_i(h_m-1)$. At vertex $m$ the formal first unit and second cap have
degree $d_i(1-h_m)$, and the formal first cap and second unit have degree
$d_i(1+h_m)$.

**The four maps and the Casimir.** All four maps are the explicit dual-basis
maps of the two monic coefficient forms on $B_m$: $\tau_{\mathrm{old}}:B_m\to

morphisms, with composition of maps. Every $M$ is an object of

$(A,A)$-bimodule under left and right multiplication.
